C-8.3.text: - **C-8.3** The `-o` export is a copy of the accepted deliverable published by C-8.1 after acceptance. A failed export sets `export_error` on the job and emits an event; the job stays `succeeded`. The job holds `out:<path>` from its reservation until its export is written, or until it ends without one; an export not yet written, also one a restart finishes, keeps a finished job's allocated worktree or `jobs/<id>` directory that path is in (C-8.4). Pending-export pins use the exporting job's actual `jobs.out_path`, joined by job id, beside its `out:` lease path and recorded `depends.out_path`, including for terminal legacy jobs without `depends`. Legacy discovery also carries incomplete evidence for every job holding an `out:` lease, including a job that turns terminal after the census; C-8.4's global allocated-worktree pin lasts while that lease remains. Each pass builds this off-transaction census before journal recovery can quarantine anything, and carries the same census into recovery and the archive context; if the census cannot be built, recovery makes no move that pass. Once written, the export owes nothing to the folder it was written into: when that folder is in a finished job's allocated worktree or job directory, retention may archive that tree with the exported file in it (C-8.4: the file is then in `$SUBFLEET_HOME/archive/<that job>/`, no longer at the path), while the accepted deliverable stays in the exporting job's own directory until that job is retired.

C-8.4.text: - **C-8.4** Retention: newest 500 jobs or 2 GiB (policy `retention.jobs`, `retention.bytes`), whichever binds, counted over jobs that are not conversation turns (turn jobs have their own budget, C-26.12), computed outside transactions in a maintenance pass; jobs that are active, `quarantined`, have unread notices addressed to a session, hold salvage refs referenced nowhere else, or are a gate's evidence are never pruned. A notice with no session can never be read, so it pins nothing (review IR-17). Probe and keepalive results live in `readings` and `events`, not in `jobs`. I5: a job with its own allocated worktree (writable, not in place) is protected as `turn-folder` by the archive driver's `_pin_reasons`, at selection and again before committing, while a live `worktree-turn:` or `worktree-read:` row names its recorded worktree or a folder inside it (a conversation in a repository nested there keys its row on that repository); a row on the in-place workspace keeps no in-place job, whose workspace retention never removes. A row on `jobs/<job>` or a folder inside it keeps that job, including an in-place job, because retirement moves the job directory too. Before moving either tree, `Retirement._fence_job_folder` checks turn rows, queued or live turn workdirs and live or exporting dependency users, then fences the canonical `jobs/<job>` directory atomically, including on recovery. Quarantine cleanup keeps live turn cwds and reader or turn rows, including detached jobs and quarantined attempts, and fences its location before reclaiming it. Its retirement transaction checks `folders.turn_holds` on the canonical worktree and every folder inside it before taking `retire:<job>` and `worktree:<folder>` together, and the commit transaction checks them again on the journal's canonical spelling, so a recorded worktree spelled in another case, or none recorded, does not hide a row; turn and detached-job reservation check that fence in the same store transaction, on the folder and on every folder above it (`folders.retiring`: string operations on the canonical spelling, no filesystem work), and hold writable turns, readers and detached jobs there `lease-held` until retirement releases it, also one in a repository nested inside the tree, whose row or `worktree:` lease is keyed on that repository; a retention hold for either a turn or a detached job names the fence keys as `retiring` and the folder checked, and `why` says retention is removing the finished job's tree (C-6.11). Its `leases` list names all held blockers; `retiring` names only the retention-held `worktree:` keys among them, in that order, and is omitted when none exist. The early look names retention's fences in both lists, while a reserving hold can additionally name ordinary writer or other held leases in `leases`. Every reservation fences its canonical resolved run folder in the same transaction that takes its leases. A turn has a reader row there when it differs from its Git hold; every detached job has a job-held reader row there for the whole lease lifetime, including retries and quarantined attempts. Detached launch uses that reservation's recorded resolved folder, so retargeting the submitted symlink after reservation does not redirect the provider away from its pin. These reader rows exclude no writer and do not change C-6.5's exclusive contention on the write target. Admission spells that submitted target again before reservation (`folders.present`, with the detached in-place answer taken before `_workspace`); if its pathname now resolves through a replacement symlink, the exclusive lease names the resolved folder. A read-only detached job's folder, and an allocated writer's source folder, is its workdir spelled once at submission (`folder` in `job.submitted`). Every detached admission look also spells where the workdir resolves now (`_detached_folders`, outside transactions), so a workdir replaced by a symlink into another fenced tree is checked there as well as on its recorded folder; Each modern recorded/current source carries its own absence answer to the early and reserving checks, using the same absent-name folding as row subjects independently of the row answer; no spelling is cached between looks. A legacy detached job with no recorded folder or write target uses that current spelling with NFC normalization and casefolding (`folders.retiring_folded`), including when quarantine has made its original names unspellable. This can conservatively hold a legacy job on a case-equivalent name on a volume that distinguishes case. An admission look that reaches the early fence check reads these folders before `_workspace`; a fence still present in the transaction recording the wait skips workspace preparation and runs no workspace Git. An `unspelled` in-place job can first run `_rediscovered`'s read-only lookup. Operator holds, standing pin refusals, disk and machine checks and pool ordering can hold a job earlier. A fence acquired after the early read is still checked in the reserving transaction, though workspace preparation may already have run. Fences found after the pass's lease census count as seen, so release brings the next look forward (C-6.10). An early fenced priority job keeps its priority place across tiers under a pool cap (C-6.16). Admission also checks the fences on both a turn's Git folder and its canonical actual run folder, and on every folder above either, before workspace preparation, using the same `folders.present` spelling and folded comparison for absent names as the reserving transaction, with a plain read followed, when a fence is found, by a transaction that checks the job's state and re-reads the fences. The Git folder this look reads is the one the reserving transaction names: for a turn submit could not spell in full (`unspelled`, below), the folder found again before the look, whose one answer the transaction uses too (`_rediscovered`), so a persisted `core.worktree` naming a fenced top outside the turn's folder holds the turn before its workspace is prepared (review of #141 at 2cbf6fca, P2-A). An eligible turn whose fence is still held in that transaction skips workspace preparation and runs no git in the tree being retired but, for an `unspelled` turn, that lookup: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` in its folder (a second time when git finds no checkout under a `.git`), which only reads, run without git's diagnostic trace variables (`GIT_TRACE*`, dropped from every git Subfleet's salvage helpers run, and Trace2's three targets set to `0`, which turns off a `trace2.*Target` in the global or system config too) (measured on APFS: no content, mode, mtime or ctime of the tree, its nested `.git` and index, a linked worktree's admin directory or an external top moved; a read may move an atime, which retention does not sign). When that lookup cannot finish (C-6.8), a turn whose recorded folder is fenced still waits on that fence, and any other waits for its workspace. The turn receives the hold the reserving transaction records when retention's fences are the only blockers it finds: `lease-held` on the same fence keys in the same order, the same folder named (its actual run folder when that is fenced, otherwise its Git folder), a capacity wait under the same signature (so the same backoff), and the same `waiting` row and clock. Where the transaction would also find a key retention does not hold (a detached writer's `worktree:` on a writable turn's own folder, a lease another job holds or is queued for), its hold would list that key too and its signature would cover it; the look's lists retention's fences alone, and the first look after they are let go finds the rest. This hold precedes the placement checks and refusals that follow workspace preparation. For a still eligible turn, a fence released before that transaction allows the look to proceed; a job ended or cancelled meanwhile is neither held nor prepared. The reserving transaction still checks the fences and holds a turn if retention acquired one after the early read; that look may already have prepared its workspace in the tree. An in-place writer's folder is its write target, its checkout's top level recorded at submit and spelled again at reservation (C-6.5), and a fence on that folder itself is its own `worktree:` key, contested as before; an allocated writer's write target is the worktree admission allocates for it (C-6.6). Such a job waits through the retirement. A queued job whose recorded folder, row path or dependency folds within the allocated worktree keeps that tree at the commit (`worktree-in-use`, while the job has not ended), which rolls the retirement back; submission records a job's workdir in its one spelling (`folders.canonical`), so a workdir typed in another case or Unicode form than its volume stores, or through the Data volume's firmlink (`/System/Volumes/Data/…`), still names the tree it is in, as long as every name in it can be looked up then; a name that cannot (gone, or under a directory that cannot be searched at that moment) stays as typed. Of the leases on a folder above a turn's or a detached job's, only retention's fence holds it, never a detached writer's (C-6.5). Read-only detached jobs and allocated writers take no exclusive lease on their source folder and wait there only for retention; writable turns and in-place writers retain C-6.5's contention on their exact write target. Admission spells the folder a row will name again off the store lock before its reserving transaction; detached in-place writers take this answer before `_workspace` and reuse it at reservation. It reserves a row (a turn's, or an in-place writer's `worktree:`) only on a folder whose every name it looked up (`folders.present`), so a row names its folder as the volume stores it, whatever submit recorded: a native session's cwd typed `…/jOB/vendor/lib` for the tree `Job`, spelled at submit while the tree was in quarantine, kept the names that could not be looked up as typed, and a row on it matched none of the checks above once its job had ended (review of 8a112986, finding 1); and a folder submit could not spell in full (`unspelled` in `job.submitted`, judged on the spelling submit records) is found again at admission as submit finds it, from its checkout's top level, once per look and before the look for retention's fence, whose answer the reserving transaction uses (never for a push job, C-8.5); where git finds no checkout though a `.git` is at or above the folder (its tree away for git's look), submit and admission ask git once more, so a turn submitted from a subdirectory while its tree was away still holds its checkout, not the subdirectory (C-6.5; review of 3410b4f0, P1; review of fb674463, Q1, Q1b and Q1c). A folder with a name that is not there reserves nothing: it waits `lease-held` on a retention fence it is in, compared case- and normalization-insensitively (`folders.retiring(..., folded=True)`), and its queued job keeps the tree at the commit when any of its recorded places folds within the allocated tree (`worktree-in-use`); with no such fence it waits for its workspace (C-6.8). A `worktree:` lease held by anything but the job's own retirement (`retention:<job>`) keeps the job as `worktree-lease`: one on its recorded worktree keeps any job, and one on a folder inside it keeps a job with its own allocated worktree, as a turn row does (a detached in-place writer in a repository nested there holds `worktree:<that repository>`, and its quarantined attempt leaves its job `lost` with the lease kept); the retirement transaction reads those leases on the canonical worktree and every folder inside it (`folders.exclusive_inside`, one key range) before taking the fence, and the commit transaction reads them again on the journal's canonical spelling. A job may need other places than its folder (`dependencies`): an isolated review's root (`-I -D`; `gate pr` sets it to the pull request's checkout), its `-o` path, which the daemon writes after the job ends (C-8.3), and the git storage its folder's checkout uses: for each `.git` at or above the folder, the directory it is or names (`gitdir:`), that directory's common directory (`commondir`, or the repository two levels above `worktrees/` when that file is gone), its resolved initial object directory and the object directories its alternates name, five levels deep, decoding Git C-style quoted entries (including three-digit octal bytes) before filesystem decoding and resolving relative paths against the objects directory, read from those files without running git, so a `.git` naming a directory in quarantine still names it. A checkout outside a tree can keep its repository inside one (`git -C <tree>/vendor/lib worktree add <outside>`), where every git command run in the checkout reads and writes, and where a worktree writer submitted from there registers its new worktree (N4). Submit records these, spelled once (`folders.canonical`), as `depends` in `job.submitted`, beside the folder. Alternates files are streamed completely on bytes with no whole-file cap and a 1 MiB per-line bound, 256 times a 4096-byte PATH_MAX. Alternates discovery is incomplete when an existing file cannot be read to its end, a byte line exceeds that bound, a C-quoted entry cannot be decoded, or a file disappears, is replaced or has a detected write during discovery (descriptor device/inode, size, mtime and ctime before/after reading, plus the final identity of the resolved pathname opened), or an original repository alias changes or vanishes. Discovery retains the original checkout and `.git` spellings (directory, symlink or `gitdir:` file), pointer files and their targets (`gitdir:`, `commondir` and each alternates entry), and the initial `<common>/objects` spelling beside its resolved Git-storage dependency, and resolves them again after storage traversal, outside any transaction; changed targets or pointer text record incomplete discovery. Submission and admission still accept the job, but while it is live or exporting retention retires no allocated worktree, and the pass records `dependency-incomplete` with the job id and file. `worktree-in-use` keeps a job's allocated worktree (recorded, or allocated with none recorded) while another job that has not ended needs a place that is the tree or inside it: its workdir, worktree, review root or `-o` path as its row holds them, its recorded folder or write target (or, for a job queued before the folder was recorded, the folder admission spelled, `job.folder_spelled`), or a place in `depends`; and while an export to a path there is pending (some job holds `out:<path>`), using the lease path, the holder's actual `jobs.out_path` and recorded `depends.out_path`. The same dependency census keeps `jobs/<id>` as `job-directory-in-use`, including for jobs without an allocated worktree; its fence transaction rechecks those dependencies before either rename, and the final commit transaction rechecks the journal's job-directory path before deleting rows. Places compare folded (`folders.fold`: Unicode's canonical caseless form, under which APFS finds a name), so a row's workdir typed in another case or Unicode form than the volume stores, which `Path.resolve` keeps, names the tree. The pass reads this, and so do the selecting transaction and the commit transaction, again on the fence's own spelling, by database reads alone: each job's first `job.submitted`, by job id (`events_job`), and the `out:` leases, by a range of their key with a job-key join for the actual output path (validation and the completed one-shot timing comparisons in `docs/reports/2026-10-27-retention-dependency-pins.md`). Admission reads retention's fences on each place in `depends` before preparing the workspace and in the reserving transaction, comparing normalized paths folded (`dependencies.key`, as the pin query does); a matching dependency fence holds the job `lease-held` until the retirement lets go, and hold attribution uses that same `dependencies.key` to name the blocked place and its `needs` role (C-6.11). An unspellable case or Unicode tail, including the parent of an output not yet written, therefore still finds a dependency fence on the tree or any folder above that place. Dependency fences are retention-held `worktree:` keys, read in one indexed lease-key range; each place names matching keys nearest first. A job a daemon queued before `depends` was recorded has those places read for it outside any transaction, from its row: by admission when it looks at the job, and by retention once a pass (no such job is newer than a pass), including terminal jobs holding an `out:` lease. Legacy incomplete evidence is preserved through the database-only exporter recheck, also when the job turns terminal after that census, just as recorded `depends.incomplete` is preserved. An alias swapped and swapped back within one traversal can escape revalidation, and a write leaving size, mtime and ctime unchanged inside one timestamp tick can escape the descriptor stability check; dependencies introduced after discovery are outside these observations. Git-storage discovery does not interpret `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR` or `core.worktree`. A written export keeps nothing (C-8.3): retention may archive a tree a finished job exported into. Folder-row checks compare recorded canonical spellings exactly; dependency pins and fences compare normalized paths folded, with canonical spelling established outside transactions (`folders.canonical`), never filesystem inspection under the store lock. Pruning archives first (d635, `docs/desktop/retention-archive.md`): a job's files (worktree and job directory, byte for byte as clones or copies, except a tracked file whose raw bytes are a blob a network remote's refs reach in a repository that is not scratch, read back whole, and except regenerable output: inside the entries a tool writes at the top of a worktree directory whose structure says it is a virtualenv, `node_modules`, `__pycache__` (all of it) or a tool cache carrying `CACHEDIR.TAG`, which git tracks nothing in and ignores entirely (names compared NFC-normalized and casefolded) and no nested repository holds, none of them holding a `.git`, the files a rule proves regenerable (an installed distribution's file whose sha256 its RECORD names, from a distribution uv installed from an index or a network URL; bytecode with a magic number beside its source; a tool cache's own files; nothing of `node_modules`), which are deleted with the tree and not restored, while everything else in that directory is archived), its worktree's admin directory and every object that directory names, its salvage commits and baseline (parents of one anchor commit, the only head of a bundle of every commit no network remote holds; a salvage ref whose commit the verified anchor reaches is referenced elsewhere), and its rows (`rows.json`) are written to `$SUBFLEET_HOME/archive/<job>/` and read back before the rows are deleted; after that, an entry is deleted only if its signature (ctime included) is unchanged right before the unlink, or, for a file that had other links when archived and whose ctime alone moved, only if its bytes still hash to the archived sha256, and anything new or changed goes to `$SUBFLEET_HOME/retention-conflicts/<job>/`. A salvage snapshot's skipped paths are protected unless the archive itself holds their bytes and reads them back; a caller's `salvage_referenced_elsewhere` vouch releases only the ref pin, never the file-preservation check. A regular file with neither stored bytes nor a verified omission or regenerable proof keeps the job as `protected`, with `unarchived path` and its path in the result's `deferred` reasons, never `pruned`; this check also runs before committing a resumed archive, whose journal bypasses the builder. A job whose tree another tool holds aside, or whose tree left or came back while it was being retired, is kept. A pass retires the oldest eligible jobs in a bounded batch, without sizing every job first, parks a job whose archive needs more than its slice with its progress (a slice always makes new progress, and parked jobs take turns), defers a busy or failing one (keeping what it archived; a repeated error waits longer), counts a job it cannot measure as decided, and never runs a repository-wide `git worktree prune`; the daemon retains measured sizes and archive progress between passes. While work remains, a completed batch that advances (including a newly cached size, a parked archive slice, publication, partial verified deletion, or a prune) is followed 5 s later; an advancing batch that reaches its deadline warns and raises `TimeoutError`, on C-5.10’s worker clock. A deadline with neither pruning nor advancement marks `TimeoutError`, warns once with the store’s job count, rearms the hour and does not raise. A cancelled pass marks `CancelledError` and rearms the hour even after progress. A completed pass with nothing more, or a batch with no advancement, marks and rearms the hour from its end. In every rearming outcome `_last_maintenance` is set last, after status bookkeeping, so a bookkeeping failure leaves retention due. A deadline limits new starts, never commits of verified archives; even slow pre-selection work permits one job to start and receive its archive slice. A failed batch holder scan marks `ScanFailed` and rearms the hour, even after quarantine, rollback or archive work, to avoid cycling the store against an unavailable scanner. Delivered service notices older than 14 days are pruned first, once per retention call (one bounded batch); a failure there is logged and never stops job retention. The pass builds its off-transaction legacy census before recovery, including terminal exporters, and shares it with the archive context; a census failure prevents recovery moves that pass. Recovery finishes journaled retirements before new selection and prioritizes a job left with a journal-less `retention:<job>` lease. Its events, each pool in its result and the daemon's log lines report the bytes freed (tracked files a remote holds and regenerable output, deleted without a copy) apart from the bytes moved into the archive and the bytes the archive adds (its bundle, manifest, summary and rows, and byte copies), with the net. A job whose baseline no network remote holds, and whose bundle would carry more than `retention.remote_less_history_bytes` (default 64 MiB) of history, is kept; a job registered in a repository inside another job's tree pins that job while it has rows. Retention's children run under the `utility` QoS clamp (C-5.1). Archives are kept until a person removes them.
